about.title: Avenal Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Avenal is a small Kings County community, but its roads still see their share of collisions, particularly along Rt 269, Rt 33, San Joaquin Street, and Skyline Boulevard. Public crash records show reported collisions here tend to cluster on Saturday afternoons, between 4 and 6 p.m., when local and passing traffic overlap. Even a low-speed impact on these roads can leave someone with real injuries and real bills. If you were hurt in a collision anywhere in or around Avenal, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims in this part of Kings County. We're not a law firm — we simply make the introduction so you can talk through your options with someone who understands California injury law and can look at the specifics of what happened to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Dealing With the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock Is Shorter Than It Feels
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but that window shrinks dramatically — sometimes to six months — if a government vehicle or road defect was involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies to your Avenal accident before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Partial Blame Isn't the End of Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover a reduced amount for your share of the damages. An independent attorney can help make sure your percentage of fault isn't overstated by the other driver's insurer.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Work Against You
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, but anything you say can be used to minimize your claim later. Speaking with an attorney first, before you give any statement, helps protect what you're owed and preserves evidence while it's still fresh.

items.question: I was in a minor collision on Rt 33 near Avenal — is it worth talking to an attorney?
items.answer: Even collisions that seem minor at first can involve injuries that take days to show up, like whiplash or soft tissue damage. Talking with an independent attorney costs you nothing through LawProactive, and they can help you understand whether your situation warrants a claim. There's no obligation, and it's better to ask early than to find out later you missed a deadline.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Kings County?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit, but that deadline can be as short as six months if your claim involves a government entity, such as a public road or a government-owned vehicle. Because Avenal's roads include state routes like Rt 33 and Rt 269, it's worth having an attorney check which timeline applies to your case.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you were partially responsible for the crash — your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. Insurance companies sometimes try to shift more blame onto you than is fair, so having an independent attorney review the details can help protect your claim.
